ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a statistical chart of urbanization development for the world and Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America. Bars represent the 2010 urbanization level, and the line represents the average urbanization speed. North America and Europe have relatively high urbanization levels but relatively low urbanization speeds; Asia and Africa have relatively low urbanization levels but relatively fast urbanization speeds, which conforms to the characteristics of rapid urbanization in emerging regions. Reasoning: The question stem asks to judge, among the problems that appear in cities during the rapid urbanization of emerging countries, which kind of “retirement policy change” is most inconsistent with reality. The typical problems of rapid urbanization in emerging countries are mainly large numbers of rural population pouring into cities, employment pressure, tight housing and infrastructure, etc.; their background is usually not labor shortage caused by severe aging. Delaying retirement age is generally more common in countries or regions with obvious population aging and insufficient labor supply, so taking “retirement age delayed” as an urban problem in the rapid urbanization of emerging countries is most inconsistent with reality.
